title: Threshold degree below full parity
statement: Let $n>0$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. If $f$ is neither the parity function on all $n$ coordinates nor its negative, then $f$ has a polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at most $n-1$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
f differs from parity on all coordinates
f differs from the negative of parity on all coordinates
